findings.source_quote: οὐ κατὰ κέλευσιν τὰς ἀποδείξεις ὑμῖν τοῦ οὕτως ἔχειν ἀνάγκη παρέχειν
findings.english_quote: We are not obliged to provide you at a command with proofs that things are so.
findings.issue: The draft adopts a possible denial of obligation on command, but does not disclose the materially different scope reading in which ἀνάγκη παρέχειν remains affirmative and οὐ qualifies κατὰ κέλευσιν: proofs must be provided, not on the basis of a command. The supplied notes neither preserve this alternative nor explain the choice. This is interpretive uncertainty, not evidence of source corruption.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-quoted note distinguishing the two scope readings and explaining the contextual basis for the chosen one. Explicitly compare the draft with the candidate: “Proofs that this is so must be supplied to you, not on the basis of a command.” Any replacement main text requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: πλὴν αὐτὸ τὸ σκεῦος κενὸν ὂν οὐκ αὐτό ἐστι τόπος, ἀλλ’ ἐν ᾧ ἐστὶν αὐτὸ τὸ κενόν, εἴπερ σκεῦός ἐστιν.
findings.english_quote: Yet the vessel itself, being empty, is not itself place; rather, if it is a vessel, place is that in which the empty vessel itself is.
findings.issue: The draft interprets αὐτὸ τὸ κενόν as “the empty vessel itself,” supplying vessel through contextual ellipsis. That is defensible, particularly given the final vessel proviso, but it conceals the recurrence of the substantival κενόν previously rendered “void.” No note records the alternative “the void itself” or explains the supplied referent. The distinction matters to the argument about whether the void, hypothetically treated as a vessel, itself occupies place.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-quoted note explaining the understood ellipsis and preserving “the void itself” as the alternative. Compare the more source-transparent candidate: “Yet the vessel itself, being empty, is not itself place; rather, place is that in which the void itself is, if indeed it is a vessel.” Preserve the conditional uncertainty; any changed wording requires fresh review.
